title: Allocation of Resources for Singapore Medical Council to Process Complaints
what_it_is: Allocation of Resources for Singapore Medical Council to Process Complaints

sections.label: SMC resources and complaint efficiency
sections.summary: SMC expanded resources and training, and 70% of 2022 complaints were concluded within the year versus 23% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: SMC has expanded its resources over the past few years to better manage their workload.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The amendments to the Medical Registration Act in July 2022, resulting in the introduction of Inquiry Committees and the ability for SMC to tap on a wider pool of chairmen for complaints-related committees, has helped improve the efficiency of SMC.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: SMC has also enhanced training for committee and tribunal members and worked with the Academy of Medicine Singapore and the College of Family Physicians Singapore to expedite the processing and completion of expert reports.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: These efforts have resulted in improvements where 70% of the complaints lodged in 2022 were concluded within the year, compared to the 23% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Health will continue to work with SMC to facilitate the timely conclusion of complaint cases.

sections.label: Investigation and complaints processes
sections.summary: Investigation and processes are needed to ascertain facts, through Inquiry Committees, Complaints Committees and the Disciplinary Tribunal.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, there needs to be some investigation and some processes to ascertain the facts, whether or not there are lessons to be learnt or actions taken.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, we have Inquiry Committees, Complaints Committees and the Disciplinary Tribunal.

sections.label: Preventing frivolous complaints
sections.summary: Care teams should engage families and patients to explain care processes so misunderstandings are resolved before formal complaints.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I think the Member has a separate point, which is whether or not there should be action taken to prevent frivolous complaints.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I think the main thing that we would need to have is a clear sense of responsibility among the care teams to engage with the families and the patients to explain the processes for their care so that, when there is a misunderstanding, this can be dealt with long before a formal complaints process is engaged with.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: That is the starting position that we have around this issue.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But we are happy to take in suggestions and optimise our processes further.
